transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I just don’t feel like doing any of the things I used to love anymore, even painting or going to my dance class. I used to be so active, but now I just can't bring myself to do much of anything.
Have you felt this way for most of the day for at least the past two years, or is this a newer change that started within the last few months?

No, it hasn't been two years; this is a newer change that started about four months ago. It really took hold of me after my youngest daughter moved away and the community center cut back its arts programs. It just feels like everything changed so quickly and I've been stuck in this heavy fog ever since.
Besides the loss of interest, have you noticed significant changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels over these past four months?

My energy levels have been incredibly low, and even simple things like getting dressed or making a quick breakfast completely wear me out to the point where I have to sit right back down. I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep or appetite, though. It is just this heavy, constant fatigue that makes everything feel like such a chore.

When you are feeling this way, are you still able to function and manage your daily responsibilities, or does this 'heavy fog' make it impossible for you to carry out your normal day-to-day activities?

It has become almost impossible to manage my daily life, and I've completely stopped going to church, my dance group, and the senior center. Most days my husband has to nudge me just to do basic things like bathe or cook. I just sit around the house all day feeling completely exhausted and useless.
Do you find that you have persistent feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt about these changes, and have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living?

Yes, I constantly feel like a useless burden and blame myself for everyone drifting away from me. It has gotten to the point where I think it would be easier for my family if I just didn't wake up, and I've even pictured taking all my blood pressure pills at once, though I haven't actually done it.
